title: RAW UNREVIEWED: recurring source seams jointly reset spelling conventions and entry structure within one hand
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. A compiler retaining habits from different exemplars could switch a bundle of orthographic choices and entry construction together while the hand remains unchanged. Require recurrence of the same two bundles in nonadjacent blocks; isolated change points or section contrasts are insufficient. This seeks source-layer boundaries without guessing source language or word meanings.

design.mechanism: A single copyist preserves exemplar-specific spelling conventions when switching source units; repeated return to a source restores the convention bundle.
design.unit: Whole bounded entries in same-hand same-section blocks, with independently marked boundaries and nonadjacent recurrence.
design.contrast: Shared latent source state jointly predicting orthography and entry construction versus topic-only mixture, positional writing effects, hand-only model and independent states for both channels.
design.prediction: State inferred from one prespecified channel predicts an independently defined second channel across nonadjacent leaves; coupled resets recur beyond what section, layout, local repetition and entry size explain.
design.scope: RAW proposal only. IDEA000120/121 source montage/redaction are related but require named source passages/global code; this is source-free detection of recurring orthographic-construction seams. Legacy paragraph-mode and renderer-switch history must be checked; no renderer glosses reused. Positive structural coupling would not by itself prove source change, translation or chronology.
